## Statement

Let $(\mathsf X,\mathcal X)$ be countably generated, let $\mu$ be a nonzero $\sigma$-finite measure, and let $K$ be a probability kernel. There are a jointly measurable $p:\mathsf X\times\mathsf X\to[0,\infty]$ and a subprobability kernel $S$ such that
$$K(x,A)=\int_Ap(x,y)\,\mu(dy)+S(x,A),$$
where $S(x,\cdot)$ and $\mu$ are mutually singular for each $x$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The countably generated space, $\sigma$-finite reference measure, and probability kernel in the Statement.

[F1] [[def-measurable-space]]: a countable generating family yields an increasing sequence of finite partitions generating $\mathcal X$.

[F2] [[def-measure-kernel-and-probability-kernel]]: $x\mapsto K(x,A)$ is measurable and $K(x,\cdot)$ is a probability measure.

[F3] [[thm-lebesgue-decomposition-exists-for-sigma-finite-signed-measures]] and [[thm-radon-nikodym-density-exists-and-is-unique-up-to-almost-everywhere-equality]]: each fixed kernel section has a scalar Lebesgue decomposition and an absolutely continuous density.

[F4] [[thm-doob-submartingale-convergence]] gives almost-sure convergence for a submartingale whose positive parts have uniformly bounded expectations. [[thm-levy-upward-convergence-of-conditional-expectations]] identifies the almost-sure limit of conditional expectations along an increasing generating sequence with the conditional expectation on the generated sigma-algebra.

[F5] [[thm-measurability-of-integration-against-a-kernel]]: integrating a nonnegative jointly measurable function against a kernel preserves measurability.

[F6] [[lem-finite-measure-sets-are-approximable-by-a-generating-algebra]]: under a finite measure, every measurable set is approximable in symmetric difference by members of a generating algebra.

[F7] [[def-finite-sigma-finite-and-semifinite-measures]]: a sigma-finite measure admits a countable partition into finite-measure pieces.

[F8] [[def-measure-with-density]]: integrating a nonnegative measurable density against the reference measure defines a measure.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: select sectionwise RN decompositions and singular support sets; these are the stated representative choices.

## Proof

**Given:** The hypotheses and facts [F1]–[F7], with [A1].

1.1 Choose a disjoint measurable partition $(E_j)_{j\ge1}$ with $\mu(E_j)<\infty$ and positive total measure. Set $c_j=2^{-j}/(1+\mu(E_j))$ and $c=\sum_jc_j\mu(E_j)$. Then $0<c<\infty$, and $\bar\mu(A)=c^{-1}\sum_jc_j\mu(A\cap E_j)$ is an equivalent probability measure. Its density $w=c_j/c$ on $E_j$ is positive. For each fixed $x$, choose $K(x,\cdot)=f_x\bar\mu+S_x$ from [F3]. Let $(\mathcal P_n)$ be increasing finite partitions generating $\mathcal X$, and set
$$f_n(x,y)=\sum_{B\in\mathcal P_n:\bar\mu(B)>0}\frac{K(x,B)}{\bar\mu(B)}1_B(y),$$
with value zero on zero-measure cells. For a positive-measure cell $B\in\mathcal P_n$, its average at level $n+1$ integrates over $B$ to the sum of $K(x,C)$ over the positive-measure children $C\subseteq B$, which is at most $K(x,B)$; zero-measure parents and all their children have value zero. Thus $(f_n(x,\cdot))$ is a nonnegative $\bar\mu$-supermartingale. Also $\int f_n(x,\cdot)\,d\bar\mu\le K(x,\mathsf X)=1$, so $-f_n(x,\cdot)$ has uniformly bounded positive-part expectations and [F4] gives a finite almost-sure limit for $f_n(x,\cdot)$. [F1, F2, F3, F7, A1]

1.2 Define $f_\infty(x,y)=\limsup_n f_n(x,y)$, a jointly measurable extended nonnegative function; for each fixed $x$ it agrees almost everywhere with the finite limit from step 1.1. The conditional-expectation averages $g_n^x$ of the integrable density $f_x$ over $\mathcal P_n$ are defined by $g_n^x(y)=\bar\mu(B)^{-1}\int_B f_x\,d\bar\mu$ on positive-measure cells $B$, and by zero on zero-measure cells. Since $\int f_x\,d\bar\mu\le1$, [F4] gives $g_n^x\to f_x$ almost everywhere: $\mathcal P_n$ generates $\mathcal X$. Cellwise $g_n^x\le f_n(x,\cdot)$ because $\int_B f_x\,d\bar\mu\le K(x,B)$, with both averages zero on null cells. Taking limits proves $f_x\le f_\infty(x,\cdot)$ almost everywhere. [F2, F4, step 1.1]

2.1 For a cell $B$ at partition level $N$, every $n\ge N$ has $\int_Bf_n(x,y)\bar\mu(dy)\le K(x,B)$, since the positive-measure level-$n$ cells inside $B$ contribute only a sub-sum of the kernel masses of a partition of $B$. Fatou therefore gives $\int_Bf_\infty(x,y)\bar\mu(dy)\le K(x,B)$. By [F8], the left side defines a measure; Fatou at the whole space gives its total mass at most one, so both sides are finite measures. Their sum is a finite measure, and [F6] approximates any measurable set in symmetric difference under that sum; the inequality extends from the generating partition algebra to every measurable set. Choose a singular support $N_x$ with $\bar\mu(N_x)=0$ and $S_x(N_x^c)=0$. Since the left measure has density $f_\infty$ with respect to $\bar\mu$, it assigns zero mass to $N_x$. Applying the inequality to $A\cap N_x^c$ therefore gives $\int_Af_\infty\,d\bar\mu\le\int_Af_x\,d\bar\mu$. Together with step 1.2, this proves $f_\infty=f_x$ almost everywhere. [F3, F4, F6, F8, A1, step 1.2]

2.2 Since $\bar\mu(dy)=w(y)\mu(dy)$, set $p(x,y)=f_\infty(x,y)w(y)$ and $S(x,A)=K(x,A)-\int_Ap(x,y)\mu(dy)$. Step 2.1 shows sectionwise that $S(x,\cdot)=S_x$, a nonnegative subprobability measure singular to $\mu$. The integral is measurable in $x$ by [F5]; hence $S(\cdot,A)$ is measurable for every $A$, and its sections are countably additive. Thus $S$ is a subprobability kernel and the decomposition holds. [F2, F3, F5, step 2.1] ∎

current_resolution.upward_supplier_statement:
Assume AC. If $(\mathcal F_n)$ is increasing, $\mathcal F_\infty=\sigma(\bigcup_n\mathcal F_n)$, and $X\in L^1$, then
$$\mathbb E[X\mid\mathcal F_n]\longrightarrow\mathbb E[X\mid\mathcal F_\infty]$$
almost surely and in $L^1$.
current_resolution.upward_supplier_argument:
1.1 By F1, F2, F3 there is $Y\in L^1$ such that $M_n\to Y$ almost surely and in $L^1$. As an almost-sure limit of $\mathcal F_\infty$-measurable variables, $Y$ has an $\mathcal F_\infty$-measurable version. [F1, F2, F3]

2.1 The union $\mathcal A=\bigcup_n\mathcal F_n$ is an algebra because the filtration is increasing. If $A\in\mathcal A$, then $A\in\mathcal F_N$ for some $N$, and for every $n\ge N$, $$\int_A M_n\,dP=\int_A X\,dP.$$ Passing to the $L^1$ limit yields $\int_A Y=\int_A X$. [step 1.1]

3.1 Let $\mathcal D=\{A\in\mathcal F_\infty:\int_A Y=\int_A X\}$. Integrability makes $\mathcal D$ a monotone class, and step 2.1 gives $\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal D$. F4 yields $\sigma(\mathcal A)=\mathcal F_\infty\subseteq\mathcal D$. Thus $Y$ has exactly the defining event integrals of $\mathbb E[X\mid\mathcal F_\infty]$, proving the result. AC has the role stated in F5. [F4, F5, step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎
